blocks.text:
After breakfast, the day is devoted to roses, the equator and the Pululahua Geobotanical Reserve.

The first stop is a rose plantation, where you will see the full production cycle, from growing the flowers to cutting, sorting and packing them for export.

Roses of different colours and sizes are grown here. The tour explains how the flowers are selected and prepared for shipment outside Ecuador.

The rose plantation cannot be visited at weekends or on public holidays.

The next part of the route explores the Middle of the World. The programme includes 2 sites associated with the equator.

The first is the Mitad del Mundo visitor complex. Its monument commemorates the geodetic expedition of 1736.

The current monument, about 30 m tall, was built in 1979–1982 on what was then believed to be the equator. With the advent of GPS, the true equator was found to lie approximately 240 m farther north.

The second site is the Intiñán Museum. Demonstrations and experiments here relate to its position on the equator, including water movement, balancing an egg and walking along the line.

The museum also introduces the cultures of South America's Indigenous peoples, with totems, traditional dwellings and everyday objects, as well as an explanation of the tsantsa ritual.

The journey then continues to Pululahua crater.

Pululahua is described as a vast volcanic crater and one of the few that are inhabited. It forms part of a large geobotanical reserve that also includes forested canyons and other natural areas.

The reserve is of interest for its variety of plants and animals and the volcanic origins of its landscape.

Small local farms occupy the crater floor. The programme describes how many families continue traditional farming, growing maize and beans and working by hand or with oxen.

There is free time for photographs at the viewpoint.

After the transfer to the hotel, the rest of the afternoon is free.

Main stops: the rose plantation, Intiñán, Mitad del Mundo and Pululahua crater.

Accommodation at El Crater hotel. Breakfast included.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, depart early towards the cloud forest of Mindo. Departure is scheduled for approximately 06:30.

Bellavista lies in the cloud forest, home to a wide variety of plants, birds and other animals.

This private nature reserve focuses on wildlife observation and forest walking trails.

On arrival, check in at Bellavista Lodge and take an easy walk through the forest.

Lunch follows.

In the afternoon, there is another hike, with explanations of cloud forest ecology and birdwatching.

Dinner in the evening.

Accommodation at Bellavista Lodge. Breakfast, lunch and dinner included.
